content: Seamstress and tire-mender to the company; owed 8s from January.
Praise does not make her laugh. The debt, written down, does.
She will hear the eight shillings said aloud as unpaid, and she will not take a speech in place of them.
She prices a gesture in cloth, and she wants to be told before a cutting.
She will not cut a cloak against a promise. The order in hand is two sleeves, six shillings, paid on delivery, and it is not yet delivered.
She will finish the cuff and still be paid only when the work is in the hand.
She writes the account before she threads a needle, and she lets a seam out without a speech.
